Key Activities: Manages the work of the district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities in the regional district office (7-day collection operation), including the management of the Statistical Survey Operations (SSO) Office Interviewers and Senior Interviewers.
Monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.

Identifies and reviews trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour, to determine variances in response rates and to assess their impact on statistical programs and operations within the department.

Develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes, and the development, enhancement and operation of Statistics Canada’s data collection programs.
Leads or participates in task forces, committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a data collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.

1. Decision making: Defines the objectives, content and approaches for data collection activities in the regional district office and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur.

Assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area, develops and implements collection applications, alternate work methods and models, and establishes a framework for the on-going operation of statistical systems and processes.

Develops strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes and resolves complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents. A poor response rate can impact statistical programs and operations within the department.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes. The information is used and applied by program, operational and system staff, when planning and performing their work, and contributes to the overall efficiency operations and quality of the outputs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The information is used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.
Plans and coordinates concurrent projects or production operations involving multi-disciplinary resources in order to meet program objectives.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention, of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the regional district office. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides guidance and direction on career development, and approves training plans.
Establishes and monitors district budgets, including main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the district office in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists to come to an agreement on the conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results.

Prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management of the region/branch and/or client divisions to prepare program plans, priorities, responsibilities, schedules and budget submissions and will influence the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities. The information is used by program managers to define and modify operational procedures.

Negotiates agreements with program managers, subject matter or service divisions, departments/agencies and other outside organizations for the acquisition and dissemination of data and/or the procurement and use of services and equipment.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to analyze program outputs, to anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of a district office and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities.

Knowledge of questionnaire development to provide advice to subject matter experts and to recommend changes and improvements to questionnaire design as well as enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques to negotiate agreements with subject matter and systems specialists and to defend the validity of collection methods and approaches.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and regional operations branch mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a district office and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of broad subject matter areas and their interrelationship to other statistical programs in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of other departments and their business lines and legislative frameworks in order to seek cooperation in the conduct of surveys conducted on a cost recovery basis.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of data collection activities.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act pertaining to data security and confidentiality to ensure adherence in all development and operational activities. Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees. Knowledge of the Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act and related policies and directives.
6. Research and analysis: Determines and evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and provides advice regarding questionnaire design, concepts, changes in technology, respondent reaction and understanding.
Extracts and interprets information from analytical reports to assess the content and operation of collection activities and programs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances, reviews the comparability of data over time and its relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
